next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Iowa Secretary of State — 2026 General Election

glance_notes.source_name: Iowa Secretary of State — Three Year Election Calendar
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: The voter pre-registration deadline for Iowa's November 3, 2026 General Election is 5:00 p.m. on October 19, 2026. Eligible voters who miss the deadline may still register and vote using Iowa's Election Day Registration process.

glance_notes.source_name: Iowa Secretary of State — Election Day
glance_notes.text: Election Day Registration: Iowa allows eligible residents to register and vote on Election Day at the polling place for their current address. Election Day registrants must prove both identity and residence.

glance_notes.source_name: Iowa Secretary of State — Absentee Voting
glance_notes.text: No-Excuse Absentee Voting: Any registered Iowa voter may request an absentee ballot. A request for a mailed ballot for the November 3, 2026 General Election must reach the county auditor by 5:00 p.m. on October 19, 2026.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: To register to vote in Iowa, you must be a U.S. citizen, be an Iowa resident and be at least 17 years old. To vote in the General Election, you must be 18 years old on or before Election Day. A person cannot vote if convicted of a felony unless voting rights have been restored, if judged mentally incompetent to vote by a court, or if claiming the right to vote in another place. Voters may submit a voter registration form to their county auditor or register online if they have an Iowa driver's license or Iowa non-operator identification card. Iowa also allows eligible residents to register and vote on Election Day.
register.glance_value: Register before the deadline or on Election Day
register.source_name: Iowa Secretary of State — Voter Registration
register.internal_note: The current Secretary of State voter-registration page directly establishes citizenship, Iowa residence, age, felony-restoration, mental-competency and single-voting-residence requirements. It also establishes paper registration through the county auditor and online registration for people with Iowa driver's licenses or non-operator IDs. Election Day Registration is independently confirmed at [https://sos.iowa.gov/voters/election-day](https://sos.iowa.gov/voters/election-day).

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use the Iowa Secretary of State's Am I Registered to Vote service to verify whether your registration is current. The state voter tools also provide your precinct and polling place. If you have questions or find information that needs correction, contact your county auditor.
check_registration.glance_value: Check with the state voter-registration lookup
check_registration.source_name: Iowa Secretary of State — Am I Registered to Vote?
check_registration.internal_note: The official lookup uses data provided by county auditors through Iowa's statewide voter registration database. The Secretary of State directs voters with registration or polling-place questions to their county auditor.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: The pre-registration deadline for Iowa's November 3, 2026 General Election is 5:00 p.m. on Monday, October 19, 2026. Eligible residents who miss the pre-registration deadline may register and vote on Election Day at the polling place for their current address. Election Day registrants must provide acceptable proof of identity and residence.
deadlines.source_name: Iowa Secretary of State — Three Year Election Calendar
deadlines.internal_note: The official Three Year Election Calendar identifies Monday, October 19 as the 2026 General Election voter pre-registration deadline and states that voter-registration deadlines shown on the calendar are at 5:00 p.m. Election Day Registration requirements are verified at [https://sos.iowa.gov/voters/election-day](https://sos.iowa.gov/voters/election-day).

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: On Election Day, Iowa voters should vote at the polling place for their precinct. Use the Iowa Secretary of State's official precinct and polling-place lookup to find the correct location for your residential address. Polling-place information for special elections should be confirmed with the county auditor because locations may be consolidated or vote centers may be used.
polling_place.source_name: Iowa Secretary of State — Registration and Polling Place Lookup
polling_place.internal_note: The official lookup provides polling-place information for regularly scheduled Primary, General and City/School elections. The Secretary of State Election Day FAQ, [https://sos.iowa.gov/voters/election-day-faq](https://sos.iowa.gov/voters/election-day-faq), states that Election Day voters need to go to the polling place for their precinct.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Iowa's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. Voters should go to the polling place for their precinct and are required to provide acceptable identification before casting a regular ballot. Eligible residents who are not already registered may register and vote at the correct polling place by proving both identity and residence. A voter who cannot provide the required identification or documentation may be offered a provisional ballot.
election_day.source_name: Iowa Secretary of State — Election Day
election_day.internal_note: Election date is verified by [https://sos.iowa.gov/three-year-election-calendar](https://sos.iowa.gov/three-year-election-calendar). The Election Day page directly establishes same-day registration and identity/residence requirements. The official Election Day FAQ, [https://sos.iowa.gov/voters/election-day-faq](https://sos.iowa.gov/voters/election-day-faq), establishes the voter-ID and provisional-ballot procedures. Polling hours are independently established by Iowa Code § 49.73.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: For Iowa's November 3, 2026 General Election, polls are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m.
polling_hours.source_name: Iowa Secretary of State — Voter and Polling Place Lookup
polling_hours.internal_note: The Secretary of State's current voter lookup expressly states that polls for all elections are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. Iowa Code § 49.73 independently establishes the General Election polling hours: [https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/publications/ICC/2026/attachments/49_ADA.pdf](https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/publications/ICC/2026/attachments/49_ADA.pdf).

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: Iowa voters may vote an absentee ballot in person before Election Day without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, in-person absentee voting begins 20 days before Election Day, on October 14, at county auditors' offices. Some counties may also provide satellite absentee-voting locations. In-person absentee voting remains available through the day before Election Day under Iowa law. Locations and hours are established locally, so voters should check with their county auditor.
early_voting.source_name: Iowa Secretary of State — Elections Accessibility FAQ
early_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly states that in-person absentee voting begins 20 days before the General Election at county auditors' offices and that some counties offer satellite locations. Twenty days before November 3, 2026 is October 14. Iowa refers to this process as absentee voting in person rather than using a separate statutory early-voting system.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee & Mail Voting
absentee_mail.content: Any registered Iowa voter may request an absentee ballot without providing an excuse. The voter must submit a signed absentee-ballot request to the county auditor and provide the required identifying information, including an Iowa driver's license or non-operator ID number or the four-digit PIN from an Iowa Voter Identification Card. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the county auditor must receive a request for a mailed absentee ballot by 5:00 p.m. on October 19. Returned domestic absentee ballots generally must reach the county auditor before the polls close at 8:00 p.m. on Election Day to be counted.
absentee_mail.source_name: Iowa Secretary of State — Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly establishes that a registered voter may request an absentee ballot and that mailed-ballot requests must be received by 5:00 p.m. 15 days before the election. For November 3, 2026, that date is October 19. The page also lists required request information. Current Iowa law generally requires ordinary domestic absentee ballots to be received before polls close on Election Day. UOCAVA ballots have separate rules addressed in military_overseas.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Iowa voters are required to show identification when voting in person. Accepted identification for an already registered voter includes an Iowa driver's license or non-operator ID, Iowa Voter Identification Card, U.S. passport, U.S. military or veteran identification, or tribal identification card or document. A registered voter who does not have an Iowa driver's license or non-operator ID may receive an Iowa Voter Identification Card without charge. A voter without the necessary identification may use the documentation allowed under Iowa's Election Day Registration procedures or cast a provisional ballot and provide the required documentation by the applicable deadline.
voter_id.glance_value: Voter ID required for in-person voting
voter_id.source_name: Iowa Secretary of State — Voter ID FAQs
voter_id.internal_note: The Election Day FAQ at [https://sos.iowa.gov/voters/election-day-faq](https://sos.iowa.gov/voters/election-day-faq) directly lists Iowa driver's license/non-operator ID, U.S. passport, U.S. military or veteran ID, tribal ID/document and Iowa Voter ID Card as acceptable identification for registered voters. Election Day registrants have a broader proof-of-identity list that can include an out-of-state ID, employer ID or Iowa high school or college student ID, but those documents should not be confused with the standard registered-voter ID list.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Iowa law requires polling places to be accessible to voters with disabilities, including the voting area, parking areas, walkways and building entrances. Each polling place has an accessible voting machine to assist voters with reading or marking a ballot. A voter who needs help marking a ballot may choose another person to assist, except the voter's employer, an agent of the employer, or an officer or agent of the voter's union. Precinct election officials may also provide assistance. Voters may also use absentee voting, including in-person absentee voting at the county auditor's office.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible polling places, equipment and assistance
accessible_voting.source_name: Iowa Secretary of State — Elections Accessibility
accessible_voting.internal_note: The current accessibility page directly establishes accessible polling-place requirements, accessible voting machines and voter-assistance rights. Additional absentee accessibility guidance is available at [https://sos.iowa.gov/voters/elections-accessibility-faq](https://sos.iowa.gov/voters/elections-accessibility-faq).

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Iowa provides special registration and absentee-voting procedures for eligible military members and overseas civilian voters. Covered voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request an absentee ballot in one step. Ballots may be delivered by mail and, when requested within the applicable deadline, may also be delivered electronically by email or fax. The Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot is available to qualifying voters as a backup for federal elections. For federal elections, a UOCAVA ballot returned by mail generally must be postmarked by the Monday before Election Day or earlier and received by the county auditor no later than noon on the Monday following Election Day. Certain eligible military voters in qualifying circumstances may return a ballot electronically under Iowa's special procedures.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA, electronic delivery and FWAB available
military_overseas.source_name: Iowa Secretary of State — Military and Overseas Civilian Voters
military_overseas.internal_note: The Secretary of State's UOCAVA materials directly establish FPCA registration and ballot requests, email/fax delivery, mail return deadlines and FWAB availability. The FPCA page at [https://sos.iowa.gov/voters/register-vote-and-request-absentee-ballot](https://sos.iowa.gov/voters/register-vote-and-request-absentee-ballot) states that requests for electronic delivery must reach the county auditor by close of business on the Monday before the election. Electronic return is limited to voters who satisfy Iowa's specific statutory criteria, including certain active-duty voters outside the United States or in designated imminent-danger areas, so the reader-facing text does not imply that all UOCAVA voters may return ballots electronically.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: A college student may choose to register to vote at the student's home address or college address, but cannot register to vote at both. Students who miss the pre-registration deadline may use Election Day Registration. On Election Day, students vote at the polling place for the precinct where they are registered. An Iowa high school or college student ID may be used as one form of proof of identity when completing Election Day Registration if it is current, valid, contains a photo and meets the state's applicable requirements.
student_voting.glance_value: Choose your home or college address, not both
student_voting.source_name: Iowa Secretary of State — Voting as a College Student
student_voting.internal_note: The dedicated Secretary of State college-student page directly states that students may register at their home address or college address but not both, confirms Election Day Registration and states that Election Day voting occurs at the precinct polling place. Important distinction: an Iowa high school or college student ID appears in the Election Day Registration proof-of-identity list, but it is not listed as one of the standard voter IDs for an already registered voter. The reader-facing language preserves that distinction.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Iowa sample ballots are prepared and published through county election officials because ballot contents vary by precinct, county, legislative district and local jurisdiction. Use the Iowa Secretary of State's voter tools to identify your precinct and county auditor, then obtain the official sample ballot or ballot information from your county auditor when it becomes available.
sample_ballot.glance_value: Get your ballot information from your county auditor
sample_ballot.source_name: Iowa Secretary of State — Elections & Voting
sample_ballot.internal_note: The Secretary of State supervises Iowa's 99 county auditors, while county auditors administer elections locally. The official 2026 General Election page at [https://sos.iowa.gov/general-election](https://sos.iowa.gov/general-election) directs users to county auditors for county candidate information. Because voter-specific ballots include county, local and district contests, the county auditor is the appropriate official source for a complete sample ballot. Reverify as counties publish finalized November ballots.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Iowa Secretary of State, Elections and Voter Registration, First Floor, Lucas Building, 321 E. 12th Street, Des Moines, IA 50319. Phone: 515-281-0145. The Secretary of State coordinates and supervises elections statewide, while Iowa's 99 county auditors administer elections locally. For questions about your individual registration, polling place, absentee ballot or local voting procedures, contact your county auditor.
contact.source_name: Iowa Secretary of State — Elections & Voter Registration
contact.internal_note: The current Secretary of State website directly verifies the Elections and Voter Registration office address and 515-281-0145 telephone number. The site states that the Secretary of State supervises Iowa's 99 county auditors in election administration. The live site masks election email addresses in retrieved text, so no email address is placed in reader-facing content without direct verification. This avoids inventing or relying on an obscured address.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Iowa Secretary of State Elections and Voting website for statewide voter registration, registration-status checks, polling-place information, absentee voting, voter identification, accessibility information and military and overseas voting. Iowa's 99 county auditors administer elections locally and are the primary contacts for individual voter records, absentee ballots, local voting locations and county-specific ballot information.
